title: fix(objectql)!: a predicate delete honours deleteBehavior for every matched row: restrict refuses, master_detail cascades, set_null clears (#26871)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XG5f9ptoMdvkj41yUX3JGGd)_

Fixes #26871

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — a predicate delete (`engine.delete(object, { where, multi: true })`, reached by a flow `delete_record` node with `multi: true` and a filter) refuses with 409 `DELETE_RESTRICTED` where it succeeded, when a row it matches is held by a `restrict` reference. Nothing is widened.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md`, `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx` and `content/docs/getting-started/common-patterns.mdx` already state `deleteBehavior` with no path exception; nothing in `skills/**` or the docs taught that a predicate delete skips it.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：按条件批量删除(`multi: true` + filter,流程的 `delete_record` 批量节点走的就是它)现在对每一条命中的记录执行与按 id 删除相同的引用检查:`restrict` 拒绝整次删除,`master_detail` 子记录级联删除,`set_null` 引用被清空。
- **为什么改**：此前批量删除直接走驱动的 `deleteMany`,完全跳过 `deleteBehavior`,流程批量删父记录会留下孤儿子记录和悬空引用,而同样的记录逐条删除会被拒绝或级联。声明了却不兑现。
- **风险与回滚**：只影响"有关系字段指向它"的对象;没有任何引用的对象仍是一条 `deleteMany`、不读行、不开事务。原来能成功的批量删除,若命中行被 `restrict` 引用,现在会 409 拒绝(整体回滚)。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**：`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` 的 `delete()` 谓词分支(`[#26871]` 段);`packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-atomic.test.ts` 的 `3b` 段;`packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/delete-record-predicate-referential-walk.integration.test.ts`。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run src/engine-cascade-delete-atomic.test.ts`,预期 19 条全绿,其中 `[#26871]` 段 6 条。
- **需要你做的**：无,席位落地。

## What changes

`ObjectQL.delete()`'s predicate arm (`multi: true`, no scalar `where.id`) now runs the by-id delete's referential walk for every row it matches. The arm lives in `delete()` in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`; `engine-delete-dispatch.ts` only re-exports the dispatch predicate and is untouched. Seat ruling arm A: no second copy of the walk, no new option on `engine.delete`, no refusal of `multi: true`.

- **Cheap when there is nothing to walk.** The arm asks the by-id branch's own question, `planCascadeAtomicity(object)`. `'none'` (no `master_detail` / `lookup` / `tree` points at the object) keeps today's single `driver.deleteMany` with the composed AST: no row read, no transaction.
- **Otherwise** it reads the matched ids through the composed, row-scoped AST (`fields: ['id']`, the write's driver options), calls the existing `cascadeDeleteRelations` for each id, then deletes exactly those rows by id (`id $in`, batches of 500). By id rather than by re-running the predicate, because the walk's own writes (a `set_null` on a self-reference) can move a row into or out of the predicate; the rows deleted are the rows walked. The answer is still the count the driver reports.
- **Atomicity is the by-id branch's.** `'atomic'` wraps the read, the walks and the delete in one `transaction()`, so a `restrict` on any matched row rolls back every cascade already done; `'split'` runs unwrapped and warns once (`warnCascadeNotAtomic`), as by id.
- Because the walk is `cascadeDeleteRelations` itself, #26864's own-cascade restrict rule (merged into this branch from `main`) applies to the predicate path with no further code.
- The `cascadeDeleteRelations` docblock line "Only runs for single-id deletes — multi/predicate deletes skip cascade" described the defect and now says the walk runs for every matched row. The `engine-cascade-delete-atomic.test.ts` case "opens no transaction when the object HAS dependents declared but the delete is by predicate" pinned the defect too; it is replaced by the predicate control on an object nothing references, and the dependents case moves to the new section, which pins one transaction.

## Tests

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-atomic.test.ts`, new section 3b (`[#26871]`, 6 cases, snapshot-rollback driver): a `restrict` on one matched row refuses the whole delete with 409 `DELETE_RESTRICTED` and rolls back the cascade already done for another matched row; `master_detail` children cascade and `set_null` lookups clear for every matched row while an unmatched parent's rows stay; the walk and the delete ride ONE transaction handle; a self-referencing `set_null` that makes another row match the predicate does not get that row deleted; a detail restricting its own master refuses (the #26718 rule, inherited); zero matched rows write nothing. Plus the predicate control: no inbound relation, one `deleteMany`, no transaction, no warning. The fake driver learned `$in` (the by-id-set delete).
- `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/delete-record-predicate-referential-walk.integration.test.ts` (new, real `ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin` + `SqlDriver` better-sqlite3 + `AutomationServicePlugin`): a flow `delete_record` with `multi: true` and a filter matching two parents. Restrict on one: the run fails, the node's answer carries `innerRefusal.code` `DELETE_RESTRICTED`, and every row (both parents, the detail and the lookup the walk reached first) is still there, counted out of the driver. No restrict: both parents' `master_detail` details are deleted, their `set_null` lookups are cleared, and the unmatched parent's rows stay.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-nested-relation-lowering.test.ts`: the "every verb that takes a where" pin recorded ONE `deleteMany` carrying the lowered filter. The ledger object has relations pointing at it, so the predicate delete now reads its matched ids first; the pin now asserts that read carries the lowered filter and that nothing is written when nothing matches. The driver still never receives the nested form.

## Acceptance notes

- **In-process `multi: true` delete callers, measured.** `plugin-auth` `removeOrganizationAuthStructure` (`sys_team_member`, `sys_user_permission_set`), `plugin-sharing` `deleteRowsForDeletedRecords` / `deleteRowsByIds` / `revokeRuleGrants*` (`sys_record_share`), `service-automation` `suspended-run-store` (`sys_automation_run`, the claim compare-and-set and its capability probe): no field in `packages/**` or `examples/**` references any of those objects (searched both the string-literal and `SystemObjectName` constant spellings), so each still plans `'none'` and keeps its single `deleteMany` and its count answer. `lifecycle-service`'s production reap deletes row by row with a scalar `where.id` (dispatched by id even beside `multi: true`); its predicate fallback is reachable only by an engine with no `find`, a two-method test double. No caller depends on the walk being skipped on an object that has rules.
- **Stale prose, outside this PR's write scope, now false or half-true:** the comment above `removeOrganizationAuthStructure` (`plugin-auth/src/organization-delete.ts`, "a multi-row delete runs no cascade"), the comment above `lifecycle-service`'s per-id reap ("by-id deletes get referential cascade handling a filter-delete would bypass"), and the `sys_organization` predicate refusal (`organizationPredicateDeleteRefusal`'s `developerMessage` "it runs no referential pass" and the `[#24948]` comment in `delete()`). The refusal itself is unchanged here; whether it stays is a seat question in the report.
- **Each matched row is walked as its own root**, the same as the bulk `deleteManyData` door deleting by id row by row: a `restrict` held by ANOTHER matched row of the same delete refuses (it is outside that root's cascade set). Unchanged from deleting the same rows by id.
- **Cost.** A predicate delete on an object with inbound relations now reads its matched ids and probes each relation per row, like N by-id deletes. No ceiling is added (none was asked); an object with no inbound relation pays nothing new.
- **Observed, not measured end to end:** neither the predicate delete nor the predicate update recomputes roll-up summaries (`priorRecord` is bound only by id). Pre-existing, unrelated to the walk; noted, not filed.
